entities.summary:
Leucon II of Bosporus, also known as Leuco, was a Spartocid ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom in 240 BC.

He succeeded his half-brother Scaetes I after Paerisades II's death, taking control of the kingdom at around 230 BC. This marked the beginning of a period of instability and power struggles within the Bosporan monarchy.

Leucon II is notable for being one of the few rulers of the Bosporan Kingdom to be mentioned in ancient Greek sources, such as those by the historian Polybius.

Leucon II of Bosporus (240 BC) was a Spartocid ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom, succeeding his father Paerisades II. The reign of Leucon II is marked by a series of conflicts with neighboring kingdoms, including the Pontic Kingdom and the Cimmerian Kingdom.

As the ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom, Leucon II played a crucial role in the regional balance of power during the Hellenistic period. His reign was also characterized by a significant increase in trade and cultural exchange between the Bosporan Kingdom and other regions of the ancient world.

The legacy of Leucon II can be seen in the continued prosperity of the Bosporan Kingdom under his successors, as well as the lasting impact of Hellenistic culture on the region.
